title: Finite reindexing identifies the normalized proper and open exchange factors
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $g:Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be an isomorphism of underlying schemes, with Cartesian pullback $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]; $g,g'$ need not be $k$-linear. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY)$ and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with induced isomorphism $\bar g:\overline X'\to\overline X$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the finite-coefficient unbounded small pro-etale derived categories and canonical adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with $A=A_n$. All squares and exchange maps are those of [def-exchange-projection] over $S=Y$. For an isomorphism $u$ among $g,g',\bar g$, write $G_u=u^{-1}$ for site reindexing [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image].

For every $M\in D(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the specified proper direct-image mate is precisely the natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}(M)=r_M:G_gRp_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*G_{\bar g}M.$$
Its underived representative, for an $A$-module sheaf $F$ and $V\to Y'$ in the small pro-etale site, is the canonical identification
$$(g^{-1}p_*F)(V)=F(\overline X\times_YV)\cong F(\overline X'\times_{Y'}V\to\overline X)=(p'_*\bar g^{-1}F)(V).$$
The transpose of $r_M$ under $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$ is $G_{\bar g}(\varepsilon_{p,M})\circ\theta_{Rp_*M}$, where $\theta:Lp'^*G_g\simeq G_{\bar g}Lp^*$ is the canonical square comparison. Thus this identifies the map for the specified derived unit and counit [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the canonical open comparison $\beta_K:G_{\bar g}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!G_{g'}K$ is the reindexing comparison, with inverse the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ transpose of
$$G_{g'}K\longrightarrow G_{g'}j^{-1}j_!K\cong j'^{-1}G_{\bar g}j_!K.$$
Consequently the specified finite compact-support exchange is exactly the ordered reindexing isomorphism $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c(K)=Rp'_*(\beta_K)\circ r_{j_!K}$, natural in $K$.

proof.text: The fixed-scalar base-change transformation is the mate of the canonical pullback square (pro_baseChange_eq_mate). Transport this equality through the canonical intrinsic module equivalences using trMate and sfSquare_transport. Changing the transported right adjoints to the published direct-image coordinates conjugates the mate by those coordinate isomorphisms. fixed_restriction_eq_baseChange identifies the middle map with the ordinary section restriction, giving proper_underived. The section formula in the statement is then definitional.

Apply the proved generic derived_mate_exact_eq_square to the intrinsic ordinary adjunctions and square. The published sfCartesianOpenPullPushAdjunction is their right-derived adjunction. intrinsic_restriction_eq_square identifies the right-derived ordinary restriction with the published proper restriction. Substitution of proper_underived therefore proves equality of the specified derived mate and that restriction.
The mate counit identity applied to the equality from Step 2 is exactly the displayed counit-transpose equation, evaluated at an arbitrary unbounded object.

For any two adjunctions with isomorphic right adjoints, the inverse of the leftAdjointUniq comparison is the inverse conjugate of that right-adjoint isomorphism; prove this by the homEquiv unit equation. The iterated-mate identity and sfOpenMate_mate then identify the inverse ordinary finiteMateOpenReindexing with sfIntrinsicOpenMate, using Step 1 for its other mate. Termwise localization and its composition isomorphisms identify their derived maps.

The ordinary mate unit equation gives the open-unit square for this inverse reindexing. Apply the proved exact_unit_square transport lemma and exactAdj_unit_Qh to the actual exceptionalOpenAdjunctions, which are the termwise localized intrinsic open adjunctions. Injectivity of their homEquiv identifies the inverse reindexing component with the displayed inverse transpose.

Unfold compactificationExchangeFromData, evaluate its whiskerings, and substitute the proper comparison from Step 2. Removing identity associators gives precisely the ordered proper/open reindexing composite. Every construction uses only underlying scheme maps.

lean.note: The proper comparison reuses sfProperOpenDerivedRestriction, whose ordinary map is the canonical fibre-product section map. The open comparison is constructed from that sectionwise right-adjoint square by leftAdjointUniq, then descended termwise; its inverse is identified with the specified derived open mate. The recorded supplied-domain compactificationExchangeFromData is specialized to the actual finite operations. The final conjunct explicitly records the underived proper section map. No boundedness or k-linearity hypothesis is imposed on the reindexing isomorphisms.
